\- **Objectives of the Study** 

The main objective of the study is to design and develop a \_\_\_\_\_(*name of system*)\_\_\_\_\_ for \_\_\_\_(*organization/company*)\_\_\_\_\_\_ . . . . . 

Furthermore, the developers aim to achieve the following specific objectives: 

1\. To analyze the existing process of \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_*(important process/processes that requires  analysis for the development of the system* )\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ in the organization to identify  inefficiencies, challenges, and opportunities for improvement.

\- **Review of Related Literature** 

Sources and Publication Date Requirements: 

∙ Local Studies – At least 5 or more sources published from 2020-2025. 

∙ Foreign Studies – At least 5 or more sources published from 2020-2025. 

Guidelines for Topic Selection: 

∙ The topics and parameters of the Review of Related Literature must be directly  aligned with the Objectives of the Study to ensure relevance and coherence.  Literature that does not contribute to addressing the study’s objectives should not  be included.  
∙ Each related literature must support one or more specific objectives of the study.  Avoid relying on only one aspect of the study; instead, cover multiple relevant  parameters that collectively contribute to achieving the research goals. 

For example, if a study focuses on developing a Sales and Inventory System, the objectives  may include: 

1\. Identifying the existing process of sales and inventory management. 2\. Determining the essential features for the system. 

3\. Conducting testing and evaluation to the system. 

4\. Preparing an implementation plan for system deployment 

In this case, the related literature should include topics such as: 

1\. **Existing Sales and Inventory Management Processes** – A review of traditional and  modern methods. 

2\. **Key Features of Effective Business Systems** – Studies on functionalities required by  users. 

3\. **Usability and Acceptability of Information Systems** – Research on testing  methodologies and user experience. 

4\. **System Implementation and Deployment Strategies** – Literature on best practices  for rolling out new software systems in organizations. 

You may include any review from a related study provided that the review: 

∙ Directly support the study’s Statement of Objectives. 

∙ Provide background and historical developments related to the research focus. ∙ Identify gaps or areas for further investigation to justify the study’s significance. ∙ Serve as evidence for the potential positive outcomes of the study. ∙ Analyze strengths and weaknesses of existing solutions to improve the study’s  direction. 

∙ Guide the research process, ensuring alignment between literature, objectives,  and methodology. 

For best results, you must use any of the following search engines in searching for  research materials online: 

a. Google Scholar (https://scholar.google.com/) 

b. Microsoft Academic (https://academic.microsoft.com/home) c. BASE (https://www.base-search.net/) 

d. CORE (https://core.ac.uk/) 

e. CiteseerX (https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/index) 

f. Science.gov (https://www.science.gov/) 

g. Springer Open (https://www.springeropen.com/)  
h. ScienceOpen.com(https://www.scienceopen.com/) 

i. Sage Open(https://journals.sagepub.com/home/sgo

**Chapter 3 – Results and Discussion** 

In the beginning of this chapter, briefly introduce what this chapter will cover. 

\- **Proposed System Flowchart** 

\* Include a diagram of the system’s workflow to illustrate how different components interact. \* Briefly describe each step or process in the flowchart to ensure clarity. 

\- **System Features and User Interfaces** 

\* List and explain the core features of the system. 

\* Provide screenshots of the User Interface (UI) with a short description of each page/module. \- **System Testing and Evaluation** 

Functional Testing  

**Purpose:** To verify if the system’s features work as intended based on requirements. **How to Execute:** 

**1\. Create Test Cases** – Define multiple test scenarios that specify the expected  behavior or outcomes for each system feature. 

**2\. Perform Manual Testing** – Execute the test cases by interacting with the system  as an end-user. 

**3\. Document the Results** – Record whether each test case **Passed or Failed**, noting  any errors or unexpected behaviors for further debugging and improvement. 

\* Start by explaining the significance of functional testing, emphasizing its role  

in ensuring that the system's features operate correctly according to requirements. 

\* List and describe the test cases used in the evaluation, specifying the expected  outcomes for each scenario. 

**\*** Describe the functional testing process. 

Performance Testing 

**Purpose:** To evaluate how the system performs under various conditions, such as speed,  responsiveness, and load capacity. 

**How to Execute:** Create Test Cases, Perform Manual Testing and then Document the  Results  
\* Start by explaining the significance of performance testing, emphasizing its  role in ensuring that the system operates efficiently under different conditions,  including varying workloads and user demands. 

\* List and describe the test cases used in the evaluation, specifying the expected  outcomes for each scenario. 

**\*** Describe the performance testing process. 

Security Testing  

**Purpose:** To evaluate how the system performs under various conditions, such as speed,  responsiveness, and load capacity. 

**How to Execute:** Create Test Cases, Perform Manual Testing and then Document the  Results 

\* Start by explaining the significance of security testing, emphasizing its role in  ensuring that the system is protected against vulnerabilities, unauthorized access, and  potential cyber threats. 

\* List and describe the test cases used in the evaluation, specifying the expected  outcomes for each scenario. 

**\*** Describe the security testing process. 

Usability Testing 

**Purpose:** To verify the system’s user-friendliness and ease of navigation. 

**How to Execute:** 

1\. **Design a Usability Survey Form** – Create a structured questionnaire that  assesses key usability aspects, such as ease of use, system efficiency, and  interface design. Use a **Likert Scale (1-5 rating)** to measure user satisfaction. 

2\. **Conduct User Interaction** – Allow expected users (e.g., target audience or  stakeholders) to explore and interact with the system. Ensure they perform  essential tasks to simulate real-world usage. 

3\. **Collect User Feedback** – Ask participants to complete the survey form based on  their experience. Encourage additional comments for qualitative insights. 

\* Start by explaining the significance of usability testing, emphasizing its role in  ensuring that the system is user-friendly, intuitive, and accessible to its intended users.  
\* Explain the evaluation criteria, for example: ease of use, interface design,  

system responsiveness, and user satisfaction. 

**\*** Describe the usability testing process. 

User Acceptance Testing (UAT)  

**Purpose:** To verify if the system meets stakeholder expectations. 

**How to Execute:** Design an Acceptability Survey Form, Conduct User Interaction and  

then Collect User Feedback 

\* Start by explaining the significance of acceptance testing, highlighting its role in  

ensuring that the system meets the specified requirements and expectations of end  

users and stakeholders before deployment. 

\* Define the key evaluation criteria, for example: system functionality, reliability,  

usability, performance, and compliance with user needs. 

\* Describe the acceptance testing process, including test planning, execution of real 

world scenarios by target users, gathering feedback, and validating whether the system  meets the required standards for final approval. 

\- **Implementation Results** 

\* Explain the deployment process, whether in a test environment, a live setting, or  

through pilot testing. 

\* Include issues encountered during implementation and how they were resolved. 

\- **Analysis of Results** 

\* Present the Analysis for Functional Testing 

 Sample Analysis Format for **Functional Testing**:

| Test Case  | Expected Output  | Actual Output  | Pass/Fail  | Remarks |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Login with   correct   credentials | User is   redirected to the  dashboard | Works as   expected | Pass  | N/A |
| Submit empty   form | System shows   validation error | No validation   error | Fail  | Add required   field validation |
| Generate   monthly sales   report | PDF is generated  successfully | Report crashes  | Fail  | Optimize report  generation |

\* After presenting the analysis briefly describe the system's success rate in Functional  

Testing. 

Calculate the success rate using the formula: 

**Success Rate** \= (Number of Passed Tests / Total Tests) × 100% 

\* Present the Analysis for Performance Testing 

 Sample Analysis Format for **Performance Testing**: 

| Test Scenario  | Expected Time  (seconds) | Actual Time   (seconds) | Pass/Fail  | Remarks |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- | ----- |
| Load homepage  (1 user) | \< 3 sec  | 2.5 sec  | Pass  | N/A |
| Process a   transaction while  the database   table contains   10,000 records | \< 5 sec  | 10 sec  | Failed  | Optimize   database queries |
| 50 users   accessing reports | \< 8 sec  | 15 sec  | Failed  | Consider caching  for faster reports |
|  |  |  |  |  |

\* After presenting the analysis, briefly describe the system's success rate in Performance Testing. 

Calculate the success rate using the formula: 

**Success Rate** \= (Number of Passed Tests / Total Tests) × 100% 

\* Present the Analysis for Security Testing 

 Sample Analysis Format for **Security Testing**:

| Security Test  | Expected   Behavior | Actual Behavior  | Pass/Fail  | Remarks |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Login with wrong  password | Show "Invalid   credentials" | Works as   expected | Pass  | N/A |
| SQL Injection   attempt in login | System rejects  malicious input | Logs in without  password | Fail  | Use   parameterized  queries |
| View admin  | Access denied  | Can access  | Fail  | Fix role-based  |

| dashboard as a  normal user |  | admin panel  |  | access |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
|  |  |  |  |  |

Testing. 

Calculate the success rate using the formula:

 Sample Analysis Format for **Usability Testing**: 

| Evaluation   Criteria | Strongly   Disagree (1) | Disagree (2)  | Neutral   (3) | Agree (4)  | Strongly   Agree (5) | Average   Score |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | ----- | :---- | ----- | :---- |
